name: Jackson Pr. 14.23: a quiet ring
description: Jackson Pr. 14.23: the same drifting circle, but now the receiver must stay quiet: at most 0.000007 per steradian in the band 0.6–1.0, about a seventh of what the charge sends alone. Two charges on opposite sides of one circle, circling together, form a dipole that never turns: their radiation at $\omega_0$ cancels. Put a second charge on the far side of the circle, circling about the same drifting centre: in the lab it moves at the drift plus its circling velocity.

reality.represents: Two charges on one circle cancel their radiation (Jackson Pr. 14.23)

remarks.detail: Charges on opposite sides of one circle, circling together, have a dipole moment that stays zero: their radiation at ω₀ cancels.
The partner must move at the drift added relativistically to its circling velocity; with Galilean addition the cancellation fails by 30 times.

remarks.line: The radiation is exact for the motion
remarks.detail: What the receiver collects is computed from the particle's computed path with the exact far-zone fields (Liénard; the spectrum from Jackson's radiation integral), and the particle feels its radiation's reaction (Landau–Lifshitz).
The charges circle in uniform crossed fields given from outside; their own fields add at the receiver, and they act on each other.
